content.title: About
content.content: Yellow bell pepper (Capsicum annuum) is the mature fruit of the plant that is commonly eaten raw. It has a bright yellow color, a sweet flavor and a crisp texture. The pepper is rich in vitamins, minerals and antioxidants, making it a popular ingredient in salads, sandwiches and snacks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yellow peppers ripen later than green ones, which gives them a sweeter taste.
All bell pepper colors (green, red, yellow, orange) are the same species, differing only in ripeness.
A 100 g serving provides more than 100% of the daily value for vitamin C.
In ancient cultures peppers were grown as ornamental plants and symbols of abundance.
There are over 30 000 varieties of bell pepper, varying in shape, color and flavor.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Carotenoids (beta‑carotene, lutein) support eye health and skin.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pepper, such as skin itching or swelling.

items.title: Food contamination
items.content: Improperly washed peppers may retain pesticide residues; thorough rinsing before consumption is recommended.

items.title: Gastro‑intestinal discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of raw pepper can cause heartburn or discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Yellow bell pepper can be eaten raw in salads, sliced for snacks, added to sandwiches and wraps. It can also be lightly sautéed or roasted, while retaining most of its nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store peppers in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, placed in a perforated bag. When kept properly they stay fresh for 1‑2 weeks. Remove any damaged areas to prevent spoilage of the remaining fruit.
